title: DNA methylation remodeling and the functional implication during male gametogenesis in rice

predicted_errors.error_location: Results section 'CMT3a and CMT3b function during male gametogenesis', paragraphs describing cmt3a pollen phenotype and BS-seq samples
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text states that 'cmt3a pollen development was arrested likely at the bicellular microspore stage' and that cmt3a mutants 'produced mainly defective pollens and were infertile'. However, the same section reports BS-seq of 'meiocyte, unicellular microspore, and sperm isolated from ... cmt3a' lines. Sperm cannot be isolated if pollen development arrests at the bicellular microspore stage before sperm formation, so these two statements are incompatible.

The abstract states that 'CMT3b functions to repress zygotic gene expression in egg'. Zygotic gene expression by definition occurs in the zygote after fertilization, not in the egg before fertilization. The claim either misidentifies the developmental stage/tissue or incorrectly describes the function; it should refer to the zygote or to post-fertilization repression.
